description: İki BİLSEM ( Bilim ve Sanat Merkezi ) öğrencisinin kurduğu bir gruptur. Tek amacımız dünyamıza yararlı olmak. Grup üyeleri: Ali Kayra Osmanoğlu ve Mir Ali Alır.
summary: The meteor seen in the introductory decor is just a visual element; behind it lies an image of the International Space Station (ISS)—the most expensive structure ever built on Earth. In the workshop section, you can select your rocket using the "change fuselage" option, and then initiate the launch by selecting "launch." The rocket first travels to Venus, where you must answer a ten trivia question. It then proceeds to Neptune before finally arriving back at Earth, where the outcome displayed on the screen depends on the answer you provided during the trivia challenge.
details: Our project was created using Scratch. It begins at the International Space Station (ISS)—the most expensive structure ever built—where a meteor appears (and only there). First, you select one of seven different rockets to launch. You then arrive at Venus, where the project explains whether or not life exists there; all the information provided is verified by NASA. Next, there is a 10-question quiz. Afterward, you reach Neptune, where it is revealed whether or not life exists there. Finally, you arrive at Earth, which is identified as a habitable environment. If you scored 6 points or higher on the quiz, you receive a congratulatory message; if you scored 5 points or lower, you are taken to a "not bad" (mediocre) screen. However, if you fail to answer even a single question, you are disqualified. We used scratch, I think it is very creativity. We searched NASA , artificial intelligence and wikipedia.
dataRefs: What is the habitable zone or “Goldilocks zone”? The habitable zone is the area around a star where it is not too hot and not too cold for liquid water to exist on the surface of surrounding planets.  Imagine if Earth was where Pluto is. The Sun would be barely visible, and Earth's ocean and much of its atmosphere would freeze. On the other hand, if Earth took Mercury’s place, it would be too close to the Sun and its water would form a steam atmosphere, quickly boiling off.  The distance Earth orbits the Sun is just right for water to remain a liquid. This distance from the Sun is called the habitable zone, or the Goldilocks zone. Rocky exoplanets found in the habitable zones of their stars are more likely targets for detecting liquid water on their surfaces. Why is liquid water so important? Life on Earth started in water, and water is a necessary ingredient for life (as we know it).  ‘Just Right’ Location, location, location — of course — but exoplanet temperature, size, and the type of star it's orbiting all play key roles in whether any exoplanet could possibly be a haven for life.
